bottom_line: In Val-HeFT, valsartan vs placebo added to background heart failure therapy reduced the combined end point of mortality and morbidity (relative risk, 0.87; 97.5 percent confidence interval, 0.77 to 0.97).
implications: These data support that, in this trial population, adding valsartan to prescribed therapy reduced the combined end point of mortality and morbidity (0.87; 97.5 percent confidence interval, 0.77 to 0.97) but did not reduce all-cause mortality (1.02; 0.88–1.18). The reduction in the combined outcome was largely associated with fewer heart-failure hospitalizations (13.8 percent vs. 18.2 percent).

major_points.text: Randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind trial in chronic heart failure.
major_points.quote: The Valsartan Heart Failure Trial (Val-HeFT) was a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind, parallel-group trial.

major_points.text: 5010 patients with NYHA class II–IV heart failure were randomized to valsartan 160 mg twice daily or placebo twice daily.
major_points.quote: A total of 5010 patients with heart failure of New York Heart Association (NYHA) class II, III, or IV were randomly assigned to receive 160 mg of valsartan or placebo twice daily.

major_points.text: The two primary end points were all-cause mortality and the combined end point of mortality and morbidity (cardiac arrest with resuscitation, HF hospitalization, or IV therapy ≥4 hours).
major_points.quote: The study was designed with two primary end points: mortality and the combined end point of mortality and morbidity, which was defined as cardiac arrest with resuscitation, hospitalization for heart failure, or administration of intravenous inotropic or vasodilator drugs for four hours or more

major_points.text: All-cause mortality did not differ between groups.
major_points.quote: Death from any cause (during entire trial) 495 (19.7) 484 (19.4) 1.02 (0.88–1.18) 0.80

major_points.text: The combined mortality–morbidity end point was significantly reduced with valsartan.
The reduction in the combined end point was predominantly driven by fewer hospitalizations for heart failure.
major_points.quote: predominantly because of a lower number of patients hospitalized for heart failure: 455 (18.2 percent) in the placebo group and 346 (13.8 percent) in the valsartan group (P<0.001).

major_points.text: Adverse events leading to discontinuation were more frequent with valsartan than placebo.
major_points.quote: Adverse events leading to the discontinuation of the drug occurred in 249 of the patients receiving valsartan (9.9 percent) and 181 patients receiving placebo (7.2 percent) (P<0.001).

inclusion_criteria.text: Men and women 18 years old or older with a history and clinical findings of heart failure for at least three months before screening.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Men and women 18 years old or older with a history and clinical findings of heart failure for at least three months before screening were eligible.

inclusion_criteria.text: NYHA class II, III, or IV and clinically stable.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Patients had heart failure of New York Heart Association (NYHA) class II, III, or IV and were clinically stable.

inclusion_criteria.text: Receiving for at least two weeks a fixed-dose drug regimen that could include ACE inhibitors, diuretics, digoxin, and beta-blockers.
inclusion_criteria.quote: To be eligible, they had to have been receiving for at least two weeks a fixed-dose drug regimen that could include ACE inhibitors, di-uretics, digoxin, and beta-blockers.

inclusion_criteria.text: Documented left ventricular dysfunction with an ejection fraction of less than 40 percent and left ventricular dilatation with LV end-diastolic short-axis internal dimension >2.9 cm/m2.
inclusion_criteria.quote: they had to have documented left ventricular dysfunction with an ejection fraction of less than 40 percent and left ventricular dilatation with an echocardiographically measured short-axis internal dimension at end di-astole greater than 2.9 cm per square meter of body-surface area.

baseline.characteristic: Background therapy (% of patients) - ACE inhibitor

criticisms.text: The adverse subgroup finding for valsartan with concomitant ACE inhibitor plus beta-blocker may represent a true interaction or chance, requiring further trials.
criticisms.quote: Clarification of whether this finding represents a true interaction or is attributable to chance must await the outcome of ongoing trials evaluating the combination of an angiotensin-receptor blocker with an ACE inhibitor and a beta-block-er.

criticisms.text: Background neurohormonal-inhibitor therapy was not controlled; subgroup analysis should be interpreted with caution.
criticisms.quote: Since this background therapy was not controlled and patients were only partially stratified according to its presence or absence at randomization (according to the use of beta-blockers but not ACE inhibitors), the data generated by this analysis must be interpreted with caution.
